description: Orchestrator performs a controlled self-handoff near a configurable token threshold (~100k) and respawns in a fresh session reading that handoff, instead of relying on Claude's silent auto-compaction.

userStories.title: Orchestrator token-budget check
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator agent, I need a deterministic way to read my own current token spend and learn whether I am at or over a configurable budget threshold, so that I can decide to write a handoff and exit before silent auto-compaction kicks in.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure function reads the orchestrator transcript usage (reusing orchestratorTranscriptPath + parseTranscriptUsage from src/transcript/usage.ts) and returns { spend, threshold, overBudget } where spend is the total in-flow tokens (input + cacheCreation + cacheRead) and overBudget = spend >= threshold.
Threshold defaults to 100_000, overridable via project.toml ([orchestrator] token_budget = N) and via the CAM_ORCH_TOKEN_BUDGET env var (env wins over toml, toml wins over default).

A thin cam surface lets the orchestrator agent invoke the check from a shell (e.g. cam status --orch-budget or a small cam orch-budget subcommand) and emit a single machine-parseable line such as CAM_ORCH_BUDGET=<spend>/<threshold> over=<true|false>; exit code 0 in both cases.
Unit tests cover: under-budget, exactly-at-threshold, over-budget, missing transcript (treated as 0 spend), env-overrides-toml, toml-overrides-default.
Does not reinvent token counting: imports parseTranscriptUsage and orchestratorTranscriptPath from src/transcript/usage.ts.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: new module src/orchestrator/budget.ts (pure function) + a tiny CLI surface (preferred: new subcommand src/commands/orch-budget.ts wired in index.ts, OR a flag on src/commands/status.ts — pick whichever requires the smaller diff). Tests under test/orchestrator/budget.test.ts. Reuse src/transcript/usage.ts (do not duplicate). Read project.toml via existing src/config/toml.ts helpers. Bun runtime: prefer Bun.file over node:fs where the surrounding code already does so. noUncheckedIndexedAccess: guard regex / array accesses. Do not register a --permission-mode flag on the new subcommand. Inject the transcript reader / env / toml reader in the pure function signature so tests don't touch real ~/.claude or process.env.

userStories.title: Orchestrator handoff schema + read/write plumbing
userStories.description: As the cam system, I need a stable on-disk schema for the orchestrator's self-handoff (.claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json) plus deterministic read/write helpers, so the orchestrator can serialize its long-lived project context before exiting and the respawned session can rehydrate from it.
acceptanceCriteria: New JSON schema file scripts/cam/orch-handoff.schema.json defining the orchestrator handoff shape: required { schemaVersion, writtenAt, reason } plus optional { projectContext, currentCycle, keyDecisions, openState, openQuestions, nextActions }. Mirrors the spirit of handoff.schema.json (per-story handoff) but scoped to orchestrator lifecycle, not story completion.

New module src/orchestrator/handoff.ts exports writeOrchHandoff(claudeDir, payload) and readOrchHandoff(claudeDir) → payload | null. Reader returns null when the file is absent; throws a clear error on schema mismatch (unknown schemaVersion or missing required field).
Writer is atomic-ish: write to a tmp file in the same dir then rename, so a half-written file never poisons the respawn.
Unit tests cover: round-trip write+read, missing-file → null, malformed-JSON → throws, schemaVersion mismatch → throws, additional unknown top-level keys are preserved on read (forward compat).
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: Files: scripts/cam/orch-handoff.schema.json (new), src/orchestrator/handoff.ts (new), test/orchestrator/handoff.test.ts (new). The handoff lives at <cwd>/.claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json (matches the existing convention of .claude/.cam-orch-session and .claude/.cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt set in src/commands/run.ts:137-145). This story is plumbing only: the orchestrator agent itself is told to populate the file in US-004. Do NOT touch the unrelated setup→orchestrator handoff in src/commands/setup.ts. No em-dash in any .md emitted (schema description strings are fine; this is JSON, but keep prose clean). noUncheckedIndexedAccess: any parsed JSON access must be guarded.

userStories.title: Respawn-on-handoff in cam run
userStories.description: As the operator who started `cam run`, I need the orchestrator pane to RESPAWN a fresh orchestrator session (new session-id, rewritten .cam-orch-session) when an orchestrator-handoff file is present at claude exit, instead of unconditionally killing the tmux session, so the long-lived orchestrator can transparently roll over context without me having to restart cam.
acceptanceCriteria: The orchestrator pane command in src/commands/run.ts is changed so that when claude exits, the wrapper inspects .claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json: if present, it generates a NEW session uuid, overwrites .claude/.cam-orch-session with it, and re-execs `claude --permission-mode bypassPermissions --session-id <new-uuid> "$(cat .cam-orchestrator-prompt.txt)"`; if absent, it falls back to the existing `tmux kill-session` teardown.

The respawn is bounded: a small respawn-counter guard (e.g. ≤ 5 consecutive respawns in the lifetime of the tmux session) prevents an infinite respawn loop if the orchestrator writes a handoff but immediately exits again; on overflow, falls through to kill-session with a clear printed reason.

--permission-mode bypassPermissions is preserved (intentional per 2026-06-06 lesson on macOS amfid; do NOT remove). No --permission-mode CLI FLAG is added to any cam subcommand (still enforced by test/no-permission-mode-flag.test.ts).

The setupOrchestratorSession function is refactored so the pane command (the respawn-aware wrapper) is built by a pure, unit-testable helper (e.g. buildOrchestratorPaneCommand({ sessionName, sessionId, promptFile, handoffMarker, maxRespawns })) returning the bash -c payload string.

Unit tests cover the builder: contains the bypassPermissions flag, contains the session-id, contains a guard reading the handoff file, contains the kill-session fallback, respects the maxRespawns cap. Spawn is injected (the existing SpawnFn pattern in run.ts) so tests assert tmux respawn-pane was called with the wrapper string, not the old direct command.
Manual end-to-end verification (operator) of a real multi-hour orchestrator respawn is captured in a separate operator story (US-004 acceptance), not here.
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
userStories.notes: File: src/commands/run.ts (modify setupOrchestratorSession around lines 121-185, specifically the agentCmd at line 155 and the respawn-pane call at lines 161-165). Add a sibling helper export buildOrchestratorPaneCommand. Tests under test/run.test.ts (extend the existing run tests). Keep the existing dashboard / menu panes untouched. The handoff-marker path is <cwd>/.claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json (matches US-002). After a successful respawn-read, the wrapper should rename the handoff file (e.g. to .cam-orch-handoff.consumed.json) so the next claude exit does not trigger another respawn off the same payload; the rename is part of the wrapper string, not a separate cam command. Reuse genSessionId injection so tests are deterministic. Bun runtime: existing code uses spawnSync from node:child_process here — DO NOT change that in this story (out of scope, surgical only). F-03: the respawn wrapper mints the fresh session uuid in bash via `uuidgen` (present at /usr/bin/uuidgen on macOS arm64); the builder unit test asserts the wrapper string contains the uuid-generation token so a missing/typo'd source is caught.

userStories.title: Boot prompt rehydration + agent self-handoff instructions
userStories.description: As the cam orchestrator agent, I need (a) my boot prompt to point me at the handoff file when one exists so I rehydrate from it instead of cold-starting, and (b) explicit instructions to monitor my own token budget periodically and write a handoff + exit when I approach the threshold, so a real long-running cycle transparently rolls over fresh context.
acceptanceCriteria: buildOrchestratorPaneCommand / buildOrchestratorBootPrompt in src/commands/run.ts is updated so the boot prompt includes a directive: "If .claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json exists, read it FIRST and rehydrate from it (it is your previous-self's serialized context); otherwise perform the cold-boot sequence in subagent-orchestrator.md."

.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md is updated with a new section ("Self-handoff lifecycle") that instructs the orchestrator to: (1) periodically (e.g. after every dispatched /cam-next or worker completion) invoke the budget check from US-001; (2) when over budget, populate .claude/.cam-orch-handoff.json via the writer from US-002 with current cycle, key decisions, open state, and next actions; (3) tell the operator one line, then exit so the wrapper from US-003 respawns it fresh.

.claude/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md edits contain NO em-dash (use colon, comma, parentheses, period; per 2026-05-20 decision). Existing em-dashes already in that file are NOT touched (surgical only).
Existing unit tests for buildOrchestratorBootPrompt are updated to assert the rehydration directive is present.

Operator end-to-end verification: a real cam run session is left to accumulate context past the threshold (or the threshold is dropped via CAM_ORCH_TOKEN_BUDGET=2000 for a quick test) and the operator confirms the orchestrator wrote .cam-orch-handoff.json, exited, and respawned with the rehydrated state visible in its greeting.

templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md (the canonical copy embedded into the binary) gets the SAME Self-handoff lifecycle section as the .claude/ copy, then `bun run embed-vendor` regenerates src/templates/embedded.ts so `cam init` in other projects installs the updated agent (without this the feature works only in cam-cli's own repo).
Vendor drift check passes (bun run embed-vendor:check)
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck)
Tests pass (bun test)
